title: Machine learning predicts next-day extubation from ICU electronic health records
summary: Using 37 electronic health record features aggregated overnight for each ICU day, XGBoost, LightGBM, logistic regression, LSTM and RNN models were built on a single-center prospective cohort (448 patients, 3,095 ICU days). The best model, an LSTM, predicted next-day extubation with AUROC 0.870 internally and 0.870 on an external community-hospital cohort (333 patients, 2,835 ICU days). Plateau pressure and Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale score were among the most informative features, and 63.8% of predicted extubations occurred within three days of true extubation. The model has not been tested in clinical deployment, and both ICUs are in one health system.
ai_technology: LSTM and gradient-boosting models on electronic health record features to predict next-day extubation

evidence.tested: Internal test and external community-hospital test of next-day extubation prediction.
evidence.unknown: Effect on care or outcomes when deployed and performance beyond one health system; full text not reviewed.
